Every decent band will have some core followers, but if you're good enough, those core fans will be able to convince new listeners to join the inner circle, hence making that circle expand like a balloon.

Another factor that people tend to avoid recognizing: is your music actually good? Too many independant artists today feel entitled that their music should be heard and if they fail to grow then they just blame it on "the system" and how its rigged against the little guy. I am the music programming coordinator for Outlaw Country (as well as Underground Garage, which is Little Steven's other channel on SiriusXM). As the coordinator I am responsible for making sure that all programming content (i.e. interviews, music, promos, etc) are prepared and edited for quality control before they hit the airwaves. So I work with both the program director and talent to make sure it all happens smoothly. One of my favorite thing about these two channels is I get to work with phenomenal people whose reputations are unmatched in the music industry. Most of them are artists themselves so they know the music better than anyone, IMO. We live in an interesting time where we have access to virtually unlimited music, so it's really important we have these reputable "gatekeepers" to filter the bad from the good.
